cards.title: Patch format specification
cards.description: Versioned JSON Schema of a patch (boxes, cables, parameters): the contract shared by the engine, the SDKs, the editor, the AI assistant and MCP. Published with its reference documentation.

tasks.title: Version 1: boxes, parameters and cables (spec/patch-format.md, read by audio-patch)
JSON Schema of the format, published with its reference documentation
Box arguments (ports computed at creation, e.g. multichannel output) and the project's own box naming conventions
Coverage-guided fuzzing of patch reading (cargo-fuzz, a versioned corpus seeded from the conformance cases), then native-versus-WebAssembly differential runs of the same inputs

Collaboration-ready identities (format version 2): box and cable identifiers unique across documents and stable for their life, generated by any client without coordination (128-bit, such as UUIDv7 or ULID, never a counter), still giving a total, deterministic order where the format orders by identifier; a documented migration from version 1's integers

Merge-friendly ordered lists: the explicit order of an outlet's cables (and any other ordered list) stored as sortable position keys (fractional indexing, ties broken by identifier), so concurrent insertions by two people merge without conflict; a document stays valid after any merge, and what it means (a cycle, a layout mismatch) is checked when the plan is built, like any patch

Patch format version 2: parameter values in binary64 (the nearest binary64 to the JSON number), the algorithm version of every box and the render rules version of the patch (spec/engine-design.md decision 29); the engine plays the versions a patch names, a box type providing every version it still supports, and refuses a version it does not support with its reason; a documented, tested migration from version 1 (binary32 values kept exactly, the current versions recorded), version 1 test files kept and migrated in CI

The format of each engine decision that adds to a patch, with the step that builds it (spec/engine-design.md, each decision's Consequences): subpatches with their block, overlap and resampling; message cables, the order of an outlet's cables and message contents; the event quantum; channel layouts; box state; the seed; external references and resources; cables between discontinuity ports; time maps, meters, grooves and transports

cards.title: Public API of the audio library, in Rust, C and TypeScript
cards.description: The engine's public interface, designed in one place and grown with each step of #12 that adds a piece of it: a low-level host API, the box contract, a toolkit of proven DSP building blocks, and a patch builder; exposed in Rust, through a C interface (functions written in Rust with the C calling convention, the bridge every other language can call), and in TypeScript over the WebAssembly module. The audio library stands alone behind it: the layer above uses it only through this interface, which costs nothing measurable against calling the engine directly, proven by the benchmarks (spec/engine-design.md decisions 32 and 33). Other languages come with the work that needs them. Stabilized and versioned by #29.

tasks.title: An API specification in spec/, completed at each step of #12 that adds a piece (host settings, events, the return path, state, hot swap, the box contract)
Low-level host API in Rust: build a plan from a graph, process blocks, send timestamped events, read the return path, save and restore state, swap plans; no_std, no allocation while processing
The box contract, versioned: what a box implements (inputs, outputs, events, state, latency, its modes), usable by built-in boxes and third-party externals

A DSP toolkit crate (engine-dsp): proven building blocks (oscillators, filters stable under modulation, smoothers, delay lines, interpolation, oversampling, envelopes, the deterministic FFT) and the math layer; the boxes are built with it
A patch builder in Rust: assemble boxes and cables in code, without writing a document
The C interface, written in Rust (extern "C"), with its header; the existing WebAssembly interface becomes one case of it; isolated, audited unsafe, checked by Miri

TypeScript over the WebAssembly module, the same functions as the C interface; decide once, for every exported function, whether parameters typed as a union of literals (a precision, a render format) are also checked at run time for plain-JavaScript callers, or the type is the proof

Every interface checked against the same test vectors and conformance hashes, a gate proving the Rust, C and TypeScript surfaces expose the same functions; and the same cost: the engine driven through each public interface counted by the instruction-count benchmarks against the same patches driven directly, by an exact comparison or a per-call allowance derived and written for each interface, never by the counts' tolerance alone (block calls, borrowed slices, no call per sample, no dynamic dispatch on hot paths)
Examples that run as tests: a native host, a page in the browser, writing a box, building a patch in code
Further languages when their work needs them (Swift and Kotlin with the mobile exports, C# for game engines, Python for research), each a thin layer over the C interface, checked on the same vectors
A C interface with handles and no lock: several engines at once, never blocking the audio thread (then a WebAssembly build with threads can be allowed)

Typed errors end to end: each operation returns only the errors it can raise (SampleRate::new, Renderer::render); error codes in the C library, exported error classes in TypeScript, each class named by the API importable through the package name and recognized by instanceof; distinct load errors (bytes that are not UTF-8, an unsupported rate, an invalid patch, a plan that cannot be built); the output stage's refusals (a case's stage error blamed on no file, the kind of a C load refused for its stage), and the limiter's channel count reported as given (refused above MAX_CHANNELS before its u16 narrowing); the cause of a failure on the audio thread kept as a field of its own
One patch loader shared by native and WebAssembly, with a differential test, and one render-format dispatch shared by audio-cli and audio-wasm

The public surface tracked, so that no change goes unnoticed: the Rust crates by cargo public-api, and the names and types each TypeScript package exports through every entry point its package.json declares, each compared with the last version, every name added or removed named in [Unreleased]

Final names of the public engine API, with a glossary; a Node entry point for the npm package; the Rust render hash takes a checked render, its channel count proven to match its samples; the engine block's names: BLOCK_SIZE, the default engine block beside ENGINE_BLOCKS, MAX_ENGINE_BLOCK and NAMED_ENGINE_BLOCK, becomes DEFAULT_ENGINE_BLOCK, and every code name of that size follows the glossary's head word, engine block (the module's engine_block_size, TypeScript's blockSize beside engineBlock), after which the vocabulary's refusal of block size needs no word about BLOCK_SIZE; the output stage's protection under one form across layers (Rust Engine::set_protected, Instance::protect, C engine_protect, the worklet command's protect, TypeScript setProtected(protect)); the limiter's state (limiting or not, crossfading toward it) named apart from its mode (LimiterMode::Protected), in every layer (TruePeakLimiter::protected, OutputStage::set_protected, engine_protect, setProtected)

Box registries valid by construction: a registry from outside the engine is checked (unique names, complete metadata) before any plan uses it; a parameter's finite range holding its default already holds by construction (ParamSpec::new)

Every native entry point that does float work (building, processing, rendering, limiting, the C functions; found by a search of every public function doing float work at that step: audio-core's Plan::build and process, Renderer, OutputStage::apply, apply_narrowing, limited, set_limiter and set_protected, TruePeakLimiter::new and set, Detector::coefficients, audio-host's Engine::new, process, set_limiter and set_protected) takes the DefaultMode proof of fpenv or opens its scope itself, so that a native call outside the processor's default floating-point mode does not compile: a proof audio-core's entry points take, or a native layer over them as the one boundary a native host uses, decided here

cards.title: Hardening from the third review
cards.description: The third review found small defects across the engine, the bindings, the tools, the tests, the pages and the documentation that no current card covers. Each step names a defect and its fix; take them by area, next to related work when a card already touches the same files.

tasks.title: Patch reading: the format version is checked after the whole document parses, so a version-2 patch is reported as an unknown field; read format first. audio-cli and the oracle skip non-.json entries of cases/ and patches/ silently; refuse them

Non-finite samples: cable and output sums keep NaN bits that depend on the target and on the build (the compiler may swap the operands of an addition); canonicalize NaN or refuse non-finite output, with a NaN-emitting test box, and reword the render-hash and patch-format specs to match. If sums keep NaN, the reduction tests that run in WebAssembly accept any quiet NaN there (its specification), never natively

Patch format spec: say how output boxes form the channels and that several are summed onto one channel by box id (the engine's rule, spec/engine-design.md decision 28), and that parameter ranges apply to the binary32 value; add a case with three output boxes and two range tests
Render hash: the three implementations accept different sample rates (whole frames are now refused alike); align the rate domains, with a refused vector per bound

Public types before the SDKs: port indices and case frames are pointer-wide (use u16 and u32), REGISTRY's type holds the box count (use a slice), and test-only items are pub (make them pub(crate)); and the other public types still pointer-wide in the host-facing reports and stage (FirstReplaced's channel, CoreError::StageChannels's plan, the latency() of OutputStage, TruePeakLimiter, Renderer, Engine and Instance, and the channels() of all of them but TruePeakLimiter (u16 already), Plan::channels, OutputStage::new's channel count (a channel type bounded by MAX_CHANNELS, shared with TruePeakLimiter::new and Plan::channels, so that no constructor of the stage accepts more than 512 or panics on allocation; tested at 512 and 513), Detector's phases, taps and delay, the C interface's engine_latency), held by a gate refusing a pointer-wide type in a public signature of the libraries, with its fixture

osc~: the 440 Hz default is retyped as a fallback instead of derived from its parameter table; the phase wrap is never tested at an increment just below 1 or at whole cycles per sample; keep one render helper and one crossing counter; compute the 750 blocks of the comment, drop the redundant test, assert the zero-output call

osc~ wording: "identical on every target" lacks the flush-to-zero caveat, "at any frequency" should be "at any accepted frequency", and the derivations misstate the subnormal threshold, the rounding sequence and 0.999; reword the oracle and the box alike

Frame limits: the 2^29-frame domain does not hold end to end (the WAV header refuses stereo above 536,870,905 frames, even without --wav; the oracle cannot read 2 GiB files); state and enforce a frames times channels limit with boundary cases; render --wav and export also hold the samples twice, up to 8 GiB: stream the WAV, or document the peak

References and records: a change of conformance/references.json or algorithms.json goes through bless, which refuses a hand edit or a repeated key and bits changed without a new version, but the commit's reason is prose: require a reason in the commits that touch either file
engine_input trusts its caller for the patch size, so memory grows to any length; return null above the patch-size limit
safe_message escapes neither the backslash nor invisible format characters, and allocates a String per character; escape them and write in place

Wasm sample views: the Float64Array and Float32Array views over WebAssembly memory read it in host byte order, while WebAssembly memory is little-endian; assert a little-endian host at create, refused with its reason (partial blocks are already copied bit for bit through a typed subarray)

Browser capture: the live subset is a hard-coded list and browser audio threads may flush subnormals; derive the subset from a case field, and state that graph mixing may turn -0 into +0 at the capture point (or capture at the processor output)

Building the wasm views once at construction instead of on every block (an interface version bump), done with DSP foundations step 1; bless the two aliased 8 kHz sine cases at the same time, since the Nyquist policy moves them

Wasm errors: out of memory blames the module, a stack-overflow RangeError passes as a rate error, onprocessorerror drops the ErrorEvent detail, the worklet prints the cause twice, and #next repeats guarded's trap conversion; map each error precisely and reuse guarded

Tap messages: missing or short tap channels are filled with silence and tap does not validate its channel count; refuse them as malformed with capture's check. The public MarkedEngineNode.create contradicts its doc: make the doc true or the method private

Wasm scripts: they print stack traces and throw inside an error listener; wrap errors in BuildError and reuse guardStreams. The test server's decisions sit in an entry point no test runs, read errors become a silent 404, EADDRINUSE crashes with a stack, it listens on localhost while the README says 127.0.0.1, and HOME=/ breaks the path-leak scan; move it into a tested serveMain and fix each

Allocation tests: the garbage-collection count has no calibrated positive control and fewer quanta run at large sizes; use equal quanta, a small semi-space and a control that allocates one object per quantum
Oracle sine budget: the a times 2^-48 evaluation budget has no derivation and is 93% used, and no test starts at a non-zero phase; write the budget and its preconditions, and test a phase near 2 pi

Roadmap board file: it is written in place (write a temporary file, then rename); parseBoard trims texts so validate passes a board the next command rewrites (refuse untrimmed text, compare with the serialization); keys are compared joined (compare as sets); step numbers and positions are unbounded and 007 is accepted; year 0000 and createdAt after updatedAt pass; the page imports board.json through the JSON plugin (parse it with JSON.parse)

Roadmap CLI: positions count from 0 and steps from 1 (make both 1-based); HELP is typed apart from its tables and the move usage omits --position (build it from the tables); editCard re-implements updateCard; emptyBoard is a test-only export
Test ports: freePort accepts any value of its variable and its tests depend on the host network; accept only an integer in 1-65535 and inject the listener

Skipped tests: the focus/skip selector misses deep chains, it["skip"], the {skip: true} option, .fails and test.fail; widen it with fixtures, and read the Vitest and Playwright reports against an allowlist of statuses so a skipped or expected-failure test fails the check
Test rules without a tool: ban vi.waitFor in unit tests, and add a lint rule that refuses an action button whose onClick does not ignore the repeated clicks of a double-click, each with a fixture

Commit messages: the commit-msg hook validates a different text from the one git records (the -v scissors, # lines with -m, trailing whitespace), [skip ci] and its variants are not refused, and the BREAKING-CHANGE footer is ignored; apply git's cleanup first and handle each
Pre-push: run the check in a detached worktree of the pushed commit instead of the working tree, and test an annotated release tag pushed through the real hook

Check runner: waits on children have no bound and no progress output while a step runs (each step's elapsed time is printed once it ends), and the tree gate does not name the file whose changes changed; bound the waits, list each file

Workflow gate: raw lines are tested against a deny-list, so quoted keys, "if :", a misplaced if: failure(), shell: and defaults:, toolchain or flag variables in env, secrets[...] and job-level permissions all pass; compare the whole file with a generated text or a strict grammar, one fixture per probe

Supply chain: the gate trims indentation and ignores exclusions (release-age and cooldown excludes, the Dependabot split, .npmrc, deny.toml ignores); the dependency gate exempts any path dependency and ignores [patch] and npm: overrides; the legacy extensionless .cargo/config is not refused; refuse each

Pinned versions: pnpm is not checked against packageManager, @types/node is not tied to the Node floor, the target list is typed twice, and the README retypes the pinned tool versions; tie each to its source with a test. Decide and record the remaining hardening options (build-script bans, strict dependency builds, the provenance of npm packages (pnpm's trust policy, which needs a pnpm newer than the pinned 10.18.3), pnpm's blockExoticSubdeps, a hardened CI runner such as harden-runner, workflow static analysis (zizmor or actionlint), repository rules, Dependabot for the pins)

Setup: the hooks are silently not installed with ignore-scripts (drop "|| true", add a preflight item for core.hooksPath), and the preflight refuses only Windows (allow macOS and Linux); mention the Linux system dependencies of the browsers (--with-deps)

Check speed, measured first: engine.wasm ships its name section (strip it, after checking that what an engine trap reports, and the browsers' stack traces that name functions from that section, keep what they need), and the hash is updated once per sample (chunk it); the mutation jobs stay half the threads, since a slice of 115 mutants ran as fast with 3 to 6 jobs: measure the knee on a larger slice, with the memory of each job; proc-macro2 optimized in the development profile (the opt-level override measured in crates/xtask/README.md, about 1 s per check), made alone, since a profile change widens every default check to every Rust mutant

Gate parsers: compare_reviews splits at the first " -- ", mutant_key does not parse line and column, an empty Stryker mutator name is accepted, changelog dates are checked for shape only, the README gate matches a prefix, crate_root misses tests/<dir>/main.rs, and coverage_locality matches a summary wording; fix each with a test

Hermetic tests: the hooks test has a hard-coded PATH, the list of local git variables misses one of git rev-parse --local-env-vars, tests use predictable temporary paths (removed whatever the outcome by a guard), and the tests that start cargo inherit the build variables of the runner they run under (the coverage wrapper, the mutation flags, the variables the preflight refuses); the local variables asserted against git's list, CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR for the paths, and those build variables removed from every command a test starts, asserted on the command

Vocabulary gate: it skips .astro, .txt and .toml, and JSON outside spec/ and conformance/, where British spellings and the old word for boxes have slipped in; "connection" is used for "cable"; digits are grouped three ways; nothing enforces the bans on other software names and the old project name; extend the gate and fix the occurrences

Doc-name gate: every backticked Rust or TypeScript name (Type::member, a test's snake_case name, a constant) in GLOSSARY.md, CLAUDE.md, spec/*.md and the READMEs resolves to a word of the tracked code, and every citation of a spec file's entry by its title (spec/benchmarks.md, "Title") to an entry or heading of that file, a spec file named before an unquoted title refused; a dated record keeps a name gone from the code only followed by its "now X" (the convention of spec/benchmarks.md); tool and command names it cannot resolve allowed by a list, each with its reason; with its fixtures

TypeScript @throws: the rule that @throws names the errors has no tool and many parsers have no tag; enable jsdoc/require-throws with a fixture. "Each lint rule is proven" covers only the policy's own rules: narrow the claim or snapshot the resolved configuration

Test assertions: error assertions are weak where the exact message is known, some tests take expected values from the module under test, the generator-check thresholds are retyped (512) with another strategy than the laws', the plan test boxes are copied and drifting, the scope has two constants for one interpolation error, and a spy on Promise.prototype.catch tests the implementation; assert exact literals, compute, share, the third such box being audio-cli's test-only nan-at~ (lib_tests.rs) beside the core's nonfinite~ and the laws' NonFinite: one shared test box crate

Shared browser test helpers: the CSP probe is written three times, the contrast and Tab helpers twice (disagreeing on WebKit Tab, and one reads a translucent color as opaque), and three matrix readers drift; move them to @poyetik/config with a findUp, and add one axe helper that also fails on incomplete results, used by the roadmap and wasm suites

A lint refusing a type parameter of an exported TypeScript function that is not inferred from a required argument (today review and a type fixture per function), with its policy fixture
Time pnpm build:wasm cold and warm, and its disk use, with one target directory per module against one shared directory, and record both in tooling/wasm-build/README.md
Remove the pnpm audit exception for GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf (picomatch ReDoS, reached only by development tools) once pnpm audit passes without it; the exception register stays empty otherwise.

A preflight per xtask command: each command checks only the tools it starts (a bless needs neither cargo-mutants, cargo-deny, the coverage, Miri nor prlimit), each tool tagged with the commands that start it and a gate keeping the tags true, and the least version of each tool the command needs where an option requires it (git 2.30 for rev-parse --end-of-options), refused with the version found

A bless log: every commit changing spec/benchmark-baseline.json adds a row (its subject, the module's bytes, the counts) to a record whose last row equals the baseline, checked by a history gate, so that spec/benchmarks.md's chain of sizes is rebuilt from it

Run the workspace's doc tests once per check: measure them, and if worth it, the step Rust tests leaves them out, the step checking their error codes being their one run, the argument (no outcome only the stable run can give) and the measurement recorded in crates/xtask/README.md

A render of a known length longer than a 32-bit target's memory: Renderer::lasting keeps the known-length report (spec/engine-design.md decision 2) without requiring its rest at once (its samples at most isize::MAX bytes, 2^31 - 1 on WebAssembly), render_rest offered only where its samples fit, with a fallible rest where they do not, as render refuses; tested at 2^31 - 1 bytes and one past, a prerequisite of an offline render in the browser (#39)

A type for every stored value of the limiter's control path built only by math::kept (zero or at least 2^-100): its stages, steps, shares, release stages and released reductions, so that an unkept stage value or step does not compile; the Hann sums, proven zero or normal instead, excepted; the frame of no change measured unchanged

The limiter's gain rounded to the nearest below a per-format reduction: derive, per output format, the reduction below which the gain may round to the nearest instead of toward zero while keeping every sample at or below the ceiling, so that a binary32 render is transparent sooner in a release tail; measure its per-frame cost; if kept, align the oracle's model of the limiter and re-bless the binary32 limited cases (before the mastering application, #39)

Run audio-core's unit tests on wasm32 (a WASI runner) and on a 32-bit target in CI: settle the pointer-wide literals of its tests and its fpenv dev-dependency (gated to the architectures fpenv supports, with the host differential), and state the targets its tests prove

Twin-copy gate: test helpers and test facts copied across crates whose tests cannot share them (hann_peak, frames_of_duration, larger, audio-core's replay of audio-host's heap phases, its signal and its order of changes, the crossfade's frames) carry a marker naming their twin, and xtask compares the marked bodies, with a fixture of a twin changed alone

Bound audio-core's coverage run: measure its instrumented unit tests per test (cargo llvm-cov, locally, on an idle machine), record them in crates/xtask/README.md, and run the heavy limiter laws that reach no line a lighter test does not in a release-built or uninstrumented target, coverage shown unchanged without them and the coverage job's time compared on one processor model

cards.title: DSP foundations: state-of-the-art audio quality before more boxes
cards.description: Set the audio quality bar before writing many boxes: objective measurements, deterministic subnormals, smoothed parameters with sample-accurate events, an allocation-free audio thread in the browser, and benchmarks.

tasks.title: Engine design decisions, recorded before any code that depends on them: messages, event scheduling, feedback, polyphony, multichannel, rates, parallelism, hot swap, latency, state; including the Nyquist policy of oscillators, an exact integer phase accumulator, the output stage (headroom, non-finite samples), the input domain of boxes, and compiling, instantiating, parsing and building plans off the audio thread, or bounding and measuring what must stay there (the construction of the engine processor), hot swap included

Objective measurements in audio-testkit and the oracle: spectrum, THD, SNR, aliasing level, with thresholds per box; spur and aliasing laws across the rate matrix; the banned float methods audited against the toolchain
Benchmarks in CI: instruction counts per box and for building large plans, with regression thresholds; the construction of the engine processor timed on the three browser engines
Deterministic strategy for subnormal numbers, proven on every target: a subnormal conformance case, and a native test with flush-to-zero forced on
Subnormal parameters treated as zero (flushed after rounding to binary32, below its smallest normal 2^-126), with the subnormal strategy, and a 1e-40 Hz oscillator case

Engine precision: binary64 processing by default and binary32 as a setting, boxes written once, generic over the sample type, all their arithmetic through the engine's math layer (the sample type, its operators and the math functions); a render hash version that records the precision and the arithmetic mode as a versioned set of option flags (all off, the strict default, the only one built), an unknown flag refused; every reference re-blessed for both precisions (a migration step), checked native and WebAssembly

Reduction order: every sum of more than two terms through one helper, 16 lanes summed in order then a fixed pairwise tree, whatever the machine's SIMD width; tested against a literal scalar reference on every target (with step 6's re-bless)

Box algorithm versions, engine side: every box type declares its algorithm version, any change of bits takes a new one, the conformance references record the versions, the render rules version and the box fingerprints they were blessed with, and check and bless refuse bits changed without a new version (the versions in the patch, playing older versions and migrating them: #3 step 7); then the end of this block (steps 6 to 8): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green
Output stage: raw and protected (safety limiter) modes; non-finite samples always replaced and reported; the playground protected by default

Host settings: sample rate, host buffer, engine block and channel counts chosen by the host, renders independent of the engine block (reduced-rate updates only on a grid of absolute frames), settings a host cannot honor reported
Patches without audio output: time advances and every box runs with zero channels, in the native renderer as in the WebAssembly engine (today one runs no box, the other runs them all)

Execution modes: live, offline and build give the same bits; every box type declares itself live-capable or offline-only, the real-time rules proven on every live-capable box, and a live plan refusing an offline-only box; then the end of this block (steps 9 to 12): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

Box contract as a public, versioned ABI shared by built-in boxes and third-party externals: explicit state, compile-friendly processing, buffers aligned to 64 bytes and padded, routing resolved when the plan is built; every built-in box giving the same bits and the same cost directly and through the ABI, the cost measured by the instruction-count benchmarks of step 3 through the interface, by an exact comparison with the direct counts or a per-call allowance derived and written for the ABI (the NaN canonicalisation of decision 25 is work per sample), never by the counts' tolerance alone (spec/engine-design.md decision 33), the plan still calling every built-in box directly and only a box type loaded at run time through one indirect call per box per block, never per sample; instantaneous responses and sub-sample discontinuity ports declared; a loaded box type's spec is 'static today (`ParamValues` holds a `&'static ObjectSpec`), so unloading one needs its own ownership decision

Typed, smoothed parameters (kinds such as frequency, with a declared Nyquist policy) and sample-accurate timestamped events, in the engine and the patch format; an event quantum per patch and subpatch (1 frame by default); a box reads its parameter values through a typed access that cannot be missing, so that no box keeps a fallback default of its own (osc~'s 440 Hz, #24 step 6)

Messages and rates: every parameter driven by messages or by an audio-rate signal; a total order of messages within a frame; MIDI input as timestamped events (MIDI 2.0 packets, MPE); then the end of this block (steps 13 to 15): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

Message payloads: trigger, number, symbol, list, MIDI 2.0 packet, note with its spelling, resource; bounded and allocation-free, symbols interned when the plan is built, typed message ports, overflow refused and reported

Control boundary: events stamped by the host (immediate or scheduled), times from other bases converted to the nearest frame by exact integer arithmetic; quotas and horizons enforced on the sending side, identical live and offline; a return path that never waits (timestamped streams, latest-value slots, engine reports, gaps reported exactly); a live event log replaying bit for bit; the output stage's live commands (the limiter's settings and its protected mode) among the commands that change bits, stamped and replayed like the others

Seeded randomness: the seed in the patch, per-box streams from stable box paths, a counter-based generator addressed by frame, exact conversion to floats, a live new-seed mode that logs its seed; its laws; then the end of this block (steps 16 to 18): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

Oscillators: an exact 64-bit integer phase accumulator; band-limited by default, with a raw variant per box; hard sync with sub-sample discontinuities. The sine's angle is reduced exactly before any rounding to binary32 (folded to the octant: the octant from the top bits of the integer phase, the rest folded exactly, so that the sine or cosine is taken of an angle in [0, π/4]), since today's binary32 osc~ rounds an unreduced angle (about 11 to 13 dB of THD+N lost, a DC offset at a quarter and half the sample rate): osc~'s binary32 thresholds and predicted THD+N tightened to match, the prediction computed from the actual angles, with a test that a quarter of the sample rate gives exactly 0, 1, 0, -1
Long-run drift check of oscillators against the exact phase, skipping ahead in state to cover hours of signal

Allocation-free audio thread in the browser, without per-frame garbage: oscilloscope through an AnalyserNode; capture and metering through a SharedArrayBuffer ring when cross-origin isolated, with a tested fallback otherwise; garbage collections while rendering measured in every browser engine, not only in V8. Until then, the tap processor behind capture and the playground oscilloscope copies every render quantum on the audio thread (a known deviation, pinned by an allocation test)

Real-time cost: estimate a patch's cost per block before it runs and report its load, so that a valid patch too heavy for real time is flagged (after the benchmarks); measure the real CPU load during playback too: the time per block in the AudioWorklet on the three browser engines and natively, on realistic patches, against the block's time budget, reported as a percentage; measure the copy of every outlet into the bus each block and remove it if it costs; break down the per-sample rounding of a binary64 render to binary32 for delivery (dac~'s binary64 count over its binary32 one) and make it cheaper if a form with the same bits costs less; then the end of this block (steps 19 to 22): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green
Silence skipping: a box declares when its output stays exactly zero, the engine skips it only then; a law that renders are identical with skipping on and off

Multichannel cables with automatic expansion and channel layouts (speaker roles and positions, ambisonic components, binaural, discrete; presets and custom layouts) checked when the plan is built; buses (sends, groups) summed in a fixed order
Deterministic FFT: one code path on every target, no run-time feature detection, twiddles from the pure-Rust libm, its error bounded against a higher-precision direct transform

Subpatches with their own block size, resampling and overlap, a block of 1 frame included; feedback cycles through an explicit delay, single-sample feedback included; delay-free loops resolved per sample (linear exactly, non-linear until a deterministic convergence test holds, at most a cap that is reported when reached), after an in-depth study of the solvers that keeps every option open

Latency declared by boxes and compensated automatically, events aligned with the compensated audio; then the end of this block (steps 23 to 27): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green
Serializable box state (presets, project save): a render saved and restored continues with the same bits
Seek law: a render that jumps to a frame with every state restored, by snapshot or replay, equals from that frame a render played from the start
Hot swap: patch edits while playing without a dropout, state transferred by box identity, optional crossfade; plans built off the audio thread, in the browser in bounded slices

Resources: content-addressed by SHA-256, immutable, decoded and resampled off the audio thread with the same code on every target, swapped at a frame, read through handles whether in memory or streamed, underruns logged; then the end of this block (steps 28 to 31): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green
Polyphony: voices per subpatch with allocation and stealing policies, MPE; polyphony through multichannel cables
Parallel graph scheduling natively, with renders identical whatever the thread count

Render-ahead hooks: future events, plan parts marked live or ahead, invalidation from a frame by restoring state; a render with render-ahead identical to one without; then the end of this block (steps 32 to 34): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

Musical time hook: per-sample transport position, tempo and time signature for boxes, tempo changes sample-accurate, through a transport box in the audio library that calls the standalone time crate of #37 (the time map and its exact evaluation: closed form and exact incremental step) instead of containing it; transports as exact time maps (tempo curves, recorded beats, irregular and additive meters, grooves, several transports, unpulsed time), the transport controls and the master clock in the coordinating layer
Audio input boxes, fed by the host
External processor boxes for third-party plugins: declared latency, imposed block size, opaque state, marked non-deterministic and excluded from hash guarantees

Clean the specification and the documentation once the engine is complete: spec/ keeps what and why (decisions, rules, laws, formats, acceptance tests), without planning (the Step and Order lines, the implementation order, what is implemented when, a section named after the ticket); the documentation describes the finished engine; then the end of this block (steps 35 to 38): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

The roadmap page and the playground served by the site

cards.title: Visual foundations: design and quality bar of the visual engine before more boxes
cards.description: The visual counterpart of #12: decide the design of a standalone visual library against the live-show targets, then set its quality and proof bar before writing many visual boxes. Like the audio library, it is usable on its own, with no dependency on the audio library or the editor; what spans sound and image lives in the coordinating layer above both. Other uses (editing, compositing, embedded) kept possible whenever it costs nothing.

tasks.title: Target matrix for the live show (node-based real-time visuals, lighting previsualization, media servers, LED pixel mapping and lasers, multi-machine shows): for each, the core concepts it needs; a target needing a new core concept is settled before any code

Engine design decisions, recorded before any code that depends on them: time and rates (the image rate carried by the render context; an image a point in time or an interval, motion blur), push and pull computation, resources and GPU memory, data types (textures, buffers, geometry including vector paths, channels, pixel aspect), color pipeline, outputs, execution modes, random access, hot swap, latency, state, algorithm versions and a spent record (the visual counterpart of spec/engine-design.md decision 29), a registry of the visual boxes, interface stability; and interaction: the input event model (the image a gesture applies to), a scene queryable on the CPU for picking, the visual box contract mapping output coordinates back to input coordinates, gesture-to-image latency, the state of interactive elements, 3D camera navigation and manipulators

The coordinating layer above the two standalone libraries (clock choice, audio and video alignment, transport controls, a scene and cues spanning both; exact musical time from the time crate, #37, sampled at every image), off the audio thread, grown from the crate #34 step 6 creates in a first form, which builds the modules a product loads: natively one binary specialized at build, in the browser one module per thread holding what that thread runs (the audio worklet the audio library's audio-thread side, never the drawing code nor this layer's asynchronous work); what this layer carries across the control boundary to align audio and video (the audio clock to the page, with the output latency) decided here; using each library only through its public interface; any hook it needs from the audio library checked against the audio engine's decisions; the architecture proven to cost nothing: benchmarks comparing work done through the public interfaces with the same work done directly, with regression thresholds
Proof tiers declared per visual box: exact (logic, CPU reference, integer GPU operations if proven), measured (floating-point GPU within derived thresholds), not guaranteed; shown by the editor
Shaders written once and translated for every GPU API; a deterministic CPU interpreter of the shader representation as the exact reference of any shader, user shaders included
Floating-point linear-light color, with color metadata (primaries, transfer, range) on every image; whether a value may exceed its alpha (emission, high dynamic range)

Objective image measurements in the test kit and the oracle (perceptual difference, color difference, aliasing, banding, flicker, and each rendered image against its ideal, unrounded shape at 10 and 12 bits per channel), thresholds per visual box with their derivation
Deterministic random access: rendering image n directly equals rendering from the start, stateful boxes through checkpoints
Video input and output in the shells: decoded images with exact timestamps, color and access cost; decoder conformance on a corpus of reference videos
Output stage: gamut and non-finite guard, and a flash limiter against photosensitive seizures
Four vertical slices on one core with no special case: raster on screen, vector paths to a simulated laser, an image mapped to DMX pixels over Art-Net, an offline render to a file
Benchmarks per visual box in CI, the image hash's own cost included, quality tiers per device, a cost estimate warning when a patch will not keep up

Desktop editor shell chosen by a measured prototype on macOS, Windows and Linux (Tauri and Electron at least): the native GPU render shown inside the editor window without copying, low-latency native audio, the interface on each system's web engine; show outputs in separate native windows

Third-party visual boxes in the editor: shaders validated by WebGPU, recovery from a lost GPU device without taking the editor down, GPU cost measured by timestamp queries, a determinism tier per shader (exact, measured, not guaranteed) with the CPU interpreter as reference, invariance to resolution and image rate and random access in the compatibility report

Interaction with the output: pointer, multi-touch, pen, keyboard and gamepad inputs of every output window as timestamped events (recorded in the event log); coordinates converted through the render chain, projection-mapping warps inverted; exact picking (CPU ray casting in 3D, point-in-shape in 2D and vector); gesture-to-image latency measured; the base for interactive web pages and creative apps as build targets, and for the interface runtime of exported apps

Further capabilities weighed in the target matrix before the design decisions: a 3D scene shared with audio (sound sources, loudspeakers, lights and projectors as elements of one scene), keyframe animation and curves, cue states and crossfades between scenes, seeded fixed-timestep particles and simulations, physically based materials and lights in photometric units shared with the light previsualization, haze and fog, dynamic quality scaling live only and reported, asset import (glTF, SVG, point clouds, images, LUTs), surtitles and captions, camera and projector calibration, keying and masks, output recording, time remapping, visual debugging, headless rendering

cards.title: Third-party boxes in the editor: sandboxed WebAssembly externals with a compatibility report
cards.description: Let anyone write boxes, as WebAssembly modules implementing the public box contract, loaded in the editor (browser and desktop) without a server. The platform is protected by construction whatever an external does; its quality stays the author's, measured and shown; a compatibility report says which features it breaks and why. Exported apps stay fully compiled: externals are translated ahead of time and proven identical by conformance.

tasks.title: Box contract expressible across a WebAssembly boundary: a stable, versioned interface, the same for built-in boxes
Loading a module in the browser and desktop editor: contract check, requested capabilities shown and granted by the user, cached by content hash, referenced by content hash in patches
Platform protections, always on: a failing external goes silent and is reported, never the host; a memory ceiling; a deterministic cost budget counted by instructions injected at load

Static determinism analysis at load: relaxed SIMD, threads and shared memory, imports beyond the contract, reads of NaN bits; NaN canonicalization and identical stack and memory limits on every engine

Determinism declared by every box and propagated through the plan; each feature (collaboration, multi-machine, replay, seek and render-ahead, conformance hashes) declares what it requires and adapts or warns; non-deterministic outputs recorded in the event log like an audio input

Compatibility report computed in the browser without a server: static analysis at once, a quick test battery in Web Workers, a deeper one in the background, cached by content hash; each failed property mapped to the features it breaks; passes stated as measurements (cases run, code coverage)
Editor display: deterministic or not and why, labels (unverified, laws passed, verified, proven), cables downstream of a non-deterministic box marked
External SDK: a Rust crate and a C header, a project template, and an external check command producing the same report
Export: externals translated ahead of time, or compiled from source when they follow the engine's rules, proven identical to the WebAssembly version by conformance
Hot reload of our own boxes in development through the same mechanism
Catalogue: the full battery across WebAssembly engines, continuous fuzzing, reproducible builds proving a module comes from its published source

cards.title: Time crate: exact musical time shared by the audio and visual libraries
cards.description: A tiny standalone no_std crate holding the time map and its exact evaluation, which the audio library, the visual library and the coordinating layer all depend on, so that every domain places a beat on the same audio frame, bit for bit, on every machine (spec/engine-design.md, decision 17). Its results are bit-defining and versioned (decision 29).

tasks.title: An exact time base: a tempo unit that represents every stated tempo exactly, and positions kept in exact integers (beats scaled by the frame rate), with no division on the path of a step
The time map and its segment kinds: constant tempo, tempo curves linear in tempo or exponential, recorded beat positions, jumps (locate, loop), each boundary rounded to a frame by decision 19's rule

Exact evaluation, by closed form at any frame and by incremental integer step, with the law that the closed form at frame n equals n steps, bit for bit, for every segment kind: a property test over random segments and frames, and the corners

Exponential tempo curves in fixed point: knots in closed form on 128-bit integers, an exact cubic stepped by integer additions between them, the knot spacing chosen per segment from its rate so that the curve stays within 2^-12 frame of the mathematical one, proven against a high-precision reference; no curve refused for its steepness

The tempo range and the register widths proven: each register's maximum derived from the stated range and checked by a test at every corner, every value out of range refused at its edge and one past it, never rounded silently

The evaluation version under decision 29: any change of the crate's results takes a new version, old versions kept; each time map records its version, and one naming an unsupported version is refused with its reason
Known-answer vectors: exact integer results per evaluation version, shared by every implementation and target

A standalone no_std crate, published like the libraries: the library gate gains its role (the only crate outside each library its crates may depend on), with its own coverage, mutation, benchmarks and conformance

cards.title: First image: a moving square, identical on every target
cards.description: The visual counterpart of #1: a white square on black, moving in time, rendered by the standalone visual library natively and in WebAssembly and shown live in the playground next to the oscilloscope. Small on purpose: it builds the whole proof chain for images (exact CPU reference, canonical image hash, conformance across targets, GPU within a measured threshold, browser tests, independent oracle) on which every visual box will then be checked. Following the sound comes with the coordinating layer above both libraries (#35 step 3).

tasks.title: Visual box contract in the standalone visual library (no dependency on the audio library), with the optional mapping from output points back to what produced them, and a square box with exact edge coverage (antialiasing)
Exact CPU reference renderer: no_std, no unsafe code, built for every target of the portability check
Canonical hash of an image sequence, specified in spec/ with known-answer vectors read by every implementation

Offline render in a visual command-line renderer and the first visual conformance case: the same hashes natively and in WebAssembly; then the end of this block (steps 1 to 4): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

GPU backend (wgpu, justified like every dependency): the same images within a measured threshold of the reference, checked in CI on a software GPU; benchmarks from this first GPU image, as for audio: the cost of rendering and of hashing, on the CPU reference and on the GPU, per image size, with regression thresholds in CI, so that each design choice from here on is measured; the subnormal and negative-zero decision for images (whether a law refuses them, what a target flushing subnormals does to the image hash), with a test that the CPU reference gives the same bits under every host floating-point mode

Playground: the square moving live next to the oscilloscope, first drawn by the CPU reference in WebAssembly; each thread loading the one module it needs, never one per library side by side (the page a module linking what it uses, the audio worklet the audio library's audio-thread side without the drawing code, since it never draws), every module built by the first form of the coordinating layer's crate (linking the libraries, with no logic spanning them yet; #35 step 3 grows it), the cost of that split measured (module size, worklet start-up, render cost); rendering into a buffer the page owns (no copy of the image per image drawn) through a package built to JavaScript with its types, then in WebGPU; an image too large for the machine refused with its size named, never a trap; the module's wrapper owning its instance by construction and taking a compiled module, as a worker receives one; the moving square accessible (reduced motion honored, a text alternative saying what it shows), with the axe audit on every state; end-to-end tests on the browsers; then the end of this block (steps 5 and 6): a deep review, its decided fixes, and a pull request whose full check is green

Independent oracle: rereads the images, recomputes the hashes and checks the motion; reads the visual cases exactly as the visual command-line renderer does, proven by a differential test over random texts
The GPU, the playground and the oracle's visual export wired into cargo xtask check (the visual conformance, coverage, Miri and the visual packages already are)
Deep review: every finding analyzed and applied, then a fresh review

cards.title: Mastering-grade audio engine: the tools of the best mastering editors and plugins on the engine
cards.description: What a mastering tool needs beyond the engine's foundations, each an addition on #12's work, none undoing a decision. Two decisions come first, since later work depends on them.

tasks.title: Decide subpatch fusion (a subpatch compiled into one box) for performance, so that a mastering chain built as a patch costs no more than dedicated boxes
Decide what to do about codecs and post-encode peak checks (AAC, MP3, Opus): excluded, through external processor boxes marked non-deterministic (#12 step 37), or a deterministic encoder of our own
Limiter: an adjustable channel link, from one linked gain to a gain per channel, its measurements derived as the linked limiter's
Limiter: 16x and 32x detector levels, their coefficients computed in the math layer and their under-read bounds derived from them, their cost benchmarked
Mid/side processing on multichannel cables (#12 step 24): a matrixing box and its exact inverse
Loudness meter after BS.1770 and EBU R128 (LUFS momentary, short-term and integrated, LRA, dBTP), its values on the return path, measured against the standard's test signals
Dither and noise shaping on seeded randomness (#12 step 18), deterministic, chosen at export, their noise spectra measured
Limiter: the gain applied oversampled against aliasing, on the resampler of subpatches (#12 step 26), its aliasing measured
Live change of the limiter's latency (maximum lookahead, detector precision) through hot swap (#12 step 30)
Multiband processing, linear-phase included, on the FFT (#12 step 25) and latency compensation (#12 step 27)
The patcher's own limiter as a patch of primitive boxes (styles, slow attacks), on subpatches and feedback (#12 step 26), tested against the output stage's limiter

cards.title: Mastering application: a professional mastering product built on the engine
cards.description: A standalone mastering application, a product of its own, at the quality and performance of the best mastering software: built on the mastering-grade engine (#38) and the patcher, on the web, on the desktop and as plugins. Its scope is decided before its code.

tasks.title: Decide the product's scope: targets (web, desktop, plugins), the chain it ships, what is built as a patch and what as dedicated boxes
Meters: loudness (LUFS momentary, short-term, integrated, LRA), true peak, spectrum and correlation, on the engine's return path
A/B comparison at matched loudness, and bypass without a click
